races.office: Tucson Unified School District Governing Board
races.notes: School board races are usually the lowest-information, highest-leverage item on the ballot.

entries.name: JoAnna Mendoza
entries.headline: Proud mom, dedicated public servant, & retired U.S. Marine.
entries.summary: JoAnna has spent her life answering the call to serve, from defending the nation and training future military leaders to helping veterans navigate broken systems. Now she is running to represent Arizona's 6th Congressional District, bringing battle-tested leadership to Washington to fight for working families and lower the costs of food, gas, housing, and child care.

entries.name: Katie Hobbs
entries.headline: Protecting democracy in Arizona
entries.summary: Governor Katie Hobbs has protected all Arizonans from a corrupt and abusive federal government. During her time in office, Katie has granted tax rebates to Arizonan families, defended reporductive rights, and passed policy to protect our water. She is running for again to continue making a positive impact on the lives of of Arizonans.

entries.name: Dr. Amelia Gallitano-Mendel
entries.headline: Tenured professor dedicated to innovative solutions
entries.summary: Dr. Gallitano is running to represent Arizona's 2nd Legislative District in the Senate. She runs as an advocate for Arizonan families and and seeks to lower the costs of every day life. She is commited to practical, evidence based solutions that will protect our future and bring integrity to the State Senate.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Kiana Maria Sears
entries.headline: Continuing more than 20 years of public service
entries.summary: As an Arizona State Senator, Kiana has been a champion for Arizonan families. She has funded nutrition programs, fought for affordable housing, and protected public education. Kiana is running to represent Arizona's 9th Legislative District in the Senate in order to continue her service.
why_bullets: Access to healthcare and nutritious meals
Access to community centered, obtainable affordable housing
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Kristie O'Brien
entries.headline: Lawyer-turned-mediator committed to Arizona
entries.summary: Kristie has centered her life around public service. After spending time working on Capitol Hill to craft policy and staff 10 senators, she came home to Arizona and serve as a lawyer to protect people's rights. Now, she is running to represent Arizona's 13th Legislative District in the Senate so that she can work to bring common-sense solutions to the table.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Elaine Aldrete
entries.headline: Experienced community leader devoted to Arizona
entries.summary: Elaine has undertaken numerous projects in her community to further the lives of those around her, including starting her non-profit Teaching Life Choices and serving as a State Committee Member. She is now running for Arizona's 16th Legislative District in the Senate to pursue advocating for affordable healthcare, housing, and utilities.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Rep. Nancy Gutierrez
entries.headline: A teacher's voice for Arizona!
entries.summary: Nancy serves as the Assistant Minority Leader in the AZ State House. She's the Ranking member on the Education Committee and is on the Appropriations Committee. She attended public school in Arizona from K-12 to earning a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education with an emphasis in Mathematics.

entries.name: Stephanie Simacek
entries.headline: Mother and representative proud to advocate for all
entries.summary: Stephanie is passionate about public education and has advocated as a state representative for tighter control Arizona's ESA program to ensure that our schools can be properly funded. Likewise, Stephanie also recognizes the lack of basic affordability impacting Arizonans and seeks to hold corporate companies accountable. To continue her service, she is running for Arizona's 2nd Legislative District in the House.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

entries.name: Karen Gresham
entries.headline: Third generation Arizonan committed to public service
entries.summary: Karen has a background in budgeting and analyzinag data as well as in public education advocacy. She has served on Madison Elementary School District's governing board and now seeks to advocate for the needs of teachers, parents, and students on a higher policy level by running for the State House as a representative of Legislative District 4.
entries.photo_credit: Arizona List / WomenCount, used with permission

organizations.name: Sonoran Rapid Response Network
organizations.description: Sample copy. A 24-hour hotline and verified responder network. When someone is detained, trained volunteers document the stop, notify family, and connect the household to legal help within the hour.
ways_to_help: Train as a legal observer - one Saturday session
Take a shift on the hotline, remote and from home
Give to the bond fund, which is always the binding constraint

organizations.name: Borderlands Legal Aid Project
organizations.description: Sample copy. Two staff attorneys and a rotating bench of volunteer lawyers covering the whole southeastern corner of the state. They take the cases nobody else in the region can take.
ways_to_help: Volunteer if you are a licensed attorney or a Spanish interpreter
Drive clients to hearings in Tucson and Phoenix
Sponsor a single case - roughly the cost of a filing fee

organizations.name: High Desert Native Vote
organizations.description: Sample copy. Registration and ballot access work across the northern counties, where a round trip to a polling place can take four hours. They run the shuttles, the translation, and the drop box monitoring.
ways_to_help: Drive a ballot shuttle route on election day
Register voters at community events, training provided

organizations.name: Valley Voter Defense Fund
organizations.description: Sample copy. Poll monitors, a same-day legal hotline, and the people who show up when a drop box is being watched by someone with a camera and a folding chair.

Give to cover the cost of election-day operations

organizations.name: Arizona Doorstep Coalition
organizations.description: Sample copy. The canvass infrastructure that the smaller groups all borrow. Turf, training, and a data operation that does not sell what it collects.
ways_to_help: Take a weekend canvass shift in your own neighborhood
Host a turf launch - coffee and a table is all it takes
Give monthly, which is what lets them hire organizers year round

organizations.name: ACLU
organizations.description: Sample copy. Eviction court accompaniment, building-level organizing, and an emergency fund that has kept a few hundred households in place. Most of their work happens the week before a hearing.
ways_to_help: Accompany a neighbor to eviction court, no legal training needed
Join a building committee where you already live
Give to the emergency rent fund
